candidate_decisions.reason: The focus clause links mercy, the conditional human return, the divine return, and an assigned confinement. Pericope cues at 17:4-7 activate the return-as-habit and reciprocal consequence; the woven-mat branch is retained as a bounded image attached to the same closing word.

The supplied 17:1 and 17:3 word coordinates match blessing, carried descent, and gratitude; these context images meet the focus Lord and mercy construction as an attributed continuity-repair reading. The inference and its alternative remain qualified.

The focus return pair is surrounded by the supplied twice-occurring corruption, restored turn, reflexive good and evil, and repeated entry. Every traced surface coordinate agrees; the self-feedback mechanism remains attributed and coexists with an externally renewed response.

The focus mercy and return construction is followed by supplied guidance, uprightness, action, repair, and reward, with a prepared painful outcome alongside them. These coordinates support an attributed path-of-correction reading without making the following ayah a grammatical gloss of the focus.

Human haste in 17:11 and counted, alternating time in 17:12 provide a distinct macro trigger for the focus return and staged-Lord branches. The proposed interval is an attributed model; the text does not state that 17:8's response is delayed.

The supplied 17:13-15 sequence attaches an outcome to each person, opens a record, makes the person read and reckon it, and denies transfer of another's burden. It supports the attributed disclosure reading while leaving historical external response intact.

The focus assignment and enclosure recur in 17:18, which adds bodily exposure, blame, and expulsion; 17:22 adds fixed posture and loss of support. All supplied coordinates agree, and the possibility that these are parallel predicates rather than stages is retained.

The focus possibility, mercy, and paired return meet supplied pericope images nominated as milk, carrying, and fullness. They support the full multi-step restoration analogy; noun-like branch restrictions remain explicit, and no literal lactation is asserted.

The focus enclosure meets 17:20's extension, gift, and explicit non-prohibition. This changes the local contrast between enclosure and withheld provision while keeping the different roots and the HFT attribution visible.

findings.title: Relapse Closed by Confinement
findings.claim: The conditional pair in 17:8 makes return both possible and consequential: mercy remains open, while renewed covering can meet a corresponding return that ends in confinement. The repeated course can also be pictured as held together within that enclosure.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are mercy at 17:8:4, the paired return at 17:8:6-7, the denier class at 17:8:10, the assignment at 17:8:8, and confinement at 17:8:11. The twice-marked history at 17:4, its reversals at 17:5-6, and the self-directed good or evil and second entry at 17:7 independently activate recurrence as habit and response. The assignment construction turns that recurrence toward an enclosing outcome; the woven-mat branch adds an image of joined repetition without replacing the confinement reading.
findings.reader_payoff: A historical return becomes perceptible as more than a repeated event: the repeated course can take spatial form in the enclosure named at the ayah's close.
findings.containment: Mercy, conditional return, and confinement remain the ordinary reading. The mat is a bounded resonance of the same form, not a claim that the destination is literally a mat; the branch does not settle how divine response relates to human return.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence and immediate pericope connections ground the cycle; the woven image is an additional lexical resonance and remains qualified.

findings.title: Carried Lineage and Repair
findings.claim: The mercy possibility can reopen continuity across generations: the lineage carried through danger and the earlier blessing make repair of a communal relation newly visible, with the prior increase in 17:6 adding a possible note of renewed growth.
findings.mechanism: Mercy at 17:8:4 is the focus carrier. The supplied blessing at 17:1 and carried descendants and gratitude at 17:3 independently meet it, while Rabb at 17:8:2 carries staged nurture. The explicit increase in wealth, children, and people at 17:6 also meets the focus Lord-carrier through the supplied increase branch, changing continuity from mere survival to possible renewed growth and response.
findings.reader_payoff: The offer of mercy can be heard as repairing a line and the relation sustained through it, with room for that line to flourish and respond again.
findings.containment: The ordinary possibility of mercy remains intact. The packet's alternative remains live: 17:1 and 17:3 may preserve blessing, lineage, and gratitude without specifying an intergenerational mechanism for 17:8. The growth branch is a contextual root resonance and does not make Rabb lexically mean increase.

epistemic.reason: The exact context surfaces and focus carriers align, but the HFT roles and the multi-step repair inference remain attributed.

findings.title: Mirrored Historical Feedback
findings.claim: The paired divine and human return can be read against 17:4-7 as a moral feedback cycle: restoration is possible, while renewed conduct can travel back toward its agents through a renewed response.
findings.mechanism: The focus verbs ʿudtum and ʿudnā carry the reciprocal motion. The two named occurrences in 17:4, the reversal of fortune and return at 17:6, and 17:7's self-directed good or harm and repeated entry independently contact that motion. Together they change a bare repetition into a return situated within the community's own renewed course.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus pair compresses a history of repeated action, reversal, and consequence into one reciprocal clause.
findings.containment: The clause still states a divine return. The attributed feedback reading does not make divine response merely automatic or self-caused; a live alternative is a sovereign renewed punishment whose historical timing does not depend on self-feedback.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic coordinates and immediate connections fit the trace, while the causal feedback relation remains an attributed inference.

findings.title: Mercy as Course Correction
findings.claim: The mercy possibility can also arrive as a usable path of correction: guidance toward upright action and repair gives the addressees a route to return differently before a prepared painful outcome is reached.
findings.mechanism: The focus mercy and return words are carriers. The immediately following guidance, uprightness, work, repair, and recompense in 17:9 independently supply a path and its result; 17:10 supplies a prepared contrary endpoint. Their contact changes mercy from an unspecified favorable possibility into an available direction of action, while the relation between adjacent ayat remains inferential.
findings.reader_payoff: The open condition can be seen to have a forward route through guidance and repair, not only a backward reference to failure.
findings.containment: Mercy and return retain their ordinary senses. The live alternative is that 17:9 begins a distinct contrast and does not explicate the mercy of 17:8. The HFT connection is attributed and does not decide whether the prepared outcome is avoidable.

epistemic.reason: The adjacent surfaces and root images match the exact trace, but their explanation of the focus as a corrective route remains attributed.

findings.title: A Measured Return
findings.claim: The answering return can also be perceived within paced governance: human haste and the passage's counted alternation allow an interval in which a harmful demand can be distinguished from a different course.
findings.mechanism: The focus Lord and return carriers meet the contrast in 17:11 between hasty human demand and wished-for good, then the alternation, counting, and detailed differentiation of 17:12. This contact changes the doubled return from an immediately mirrored reaction into an attributed model of measured response and possible discernment.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning leaves room to notice timing and discernment within the return, rather than only an instantaneous tit-for-tat.
findings.containment: The focus still states a conditional return and does not say that a delay occurs. A live alternative is that 17:11-12 concerns human haste and calendrical signs without qualifying the response in 17:8. The HFT reading remains attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT surface coordinates agree and the temporal pattern is supplied, but its application as a delay in the focus response is a contextual inference.

epistemic.reason: The focus and contextual word coordinates agree, while treating the later predicates as dimensions of one endpoint is an attributed interpretation.

The attributed milk image attached to blessing at 17:1 and the carried descendants and fullness branch at 17:3 independently meet them. Their contact changes an unspecified return of mercy into a picture of nourishment resuming through a carried line.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy and return can be perceived through the material image of sustenance becoming available again across generations.
findings.containment: The ordinary meanings of hope, mercy, and return remain. The camel and womb branches are root-level images applied by an attributed analogy, not lexical substitutions; the packet does not claim literal lactation or anatomy. The connection notes for 17:1 and 17:3 also warn that those ayat do not themselves specify the focus cycle.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace names exact supplied surfaces and a multi-step root image, but the lactational mechanism is a surprising attributed analogy.

findings.title: Unbarred Gift and Enclosure
findings.claim: The enclosure assigned for the denier class need not be read as simple withdrawal of divine provision: 17:20 describes extension and gift to both groups and says the Lord's giving is not barred.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is ḥaṣīran, with kāfirīn naming its recipients. In 17:20 the supplied extension, two recipient groups, gift, and explicit denial that giving is barred independently meet the enclosure. This changes the relation from confinement as mere deprivation to two distinct mechanisms: provision can be extended while an enclosure remains assigned.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the universal extension of gift beside the specific enclosure without collapsing them into one act of withdrawal.
findings.containment: The focus still states confinement for the denier class. The later ayah does not say that punishment is self-produced or that no one is confined; its gift and non-prohibition language adds a contrast without equating the different roots.

epistemic.reason: The exact supplied surfaces fit the trace, while the contrast between the two mechanisms remains an attributed HFT reading.

findings.title: Denial of a Granted Favor
findings.claim: The focus label kāfirīn can also carry the branch of denying a blessing: the surrounding account recalls received wealth, descendants, and increase before renewed harm and the assigned enclosure.
findings.mechanism: The focus participle at 17:8:10:3 is the carrier for the accepted blessing-denial branch. The supplied gifts and increase in 17:6, followed by the self-directed consequences in 17:7, independently trigger it. Their contact adds ingratitude toward received favor alongside the conventional religious-denial reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The final class label can be heard in relation to benefits already received within the local history, rather than only as an abstract category.
findings.containment: Religious denial and the confinement remain explicit. The contextual branch does not equate every focus recipient with every beneficiary in 17:6, or reduce kufr to ingratitude; the additional relation is qualified.

epistemic.reason: An accepted focus branch and the exact supplied historical surfaces support the contact; linking the later class label to earlier beneficiaries remains an inference.
